season.evidence: Peakbagger successful ascents: Jun 9, Jul 28, Aug 28, Sep 17, Oct 4. A search found the NPS Royal Basin season of early July to mid-October, a climbing guide preferring early July when snow still covers the ledges, and a late-June report mostly snow-free. Stored Jul-Sep kept.

track.why: The catalog holds one route on Clark (the corkscrew). This Sep 1 2025 round trip leaves from and returns to the Upper Dungeness trailhead (55 m / 35 m from our pin), passes Upper Royal Basin and Surprise Basin to the Clark-Johnson col, and its report follows the ledges to the summit (3 m from our pin). The party also climbed Johnson from the same col first, so the track includes a short Johnson side trip; 3246311 (Jun 28 2026, up only, Clark alone) is the fallback.

facts.text: By early September the Surprise Basin glacier is rock-covered and needs no axe or crampons; approach shoes cross it and the other small snowfield.
A snowfield just below the col may call for microspikes in early September; skirt it on the boulders beside it, since the choss higher up slides.
In mid-July morning snow in Surprise Basin is soft enough to climb without crampons, but the steeper slope to the col goes hard; put them on there.

notes: Single route on peak; Peakbagger summit coordinate equals our pin.
